title: How to Install the Approved Bluetooth Driver
overview: This article supports the Install the Approved Bluetooth Driver step in the Bluetooth Device Not Connecting workflow. It explains how to safely identify, obtain, and install the approved Bluetooth driver while avoiding unofficial or incompatible driver packages.
checklist: Save open work and confirm the computer model and Windows version.
Check Windows Update for available driver updates.
If the approved driver is not available through Windows Update, open Device Manager and expand Bluetooth.
Identify the correct Bluetooth adapter and confirm the computer model before downloading a driver.
Download the approved Bluetooth driver from the computer manufacturer's official support site or your organization's approved software repository.
Install the approved driver and restart Windows if prompted.
Verify that the Bluetooth adapter appears without warning icons and test Bluetooth connectivity.
Record the outcome and return to the troubleshooting workflow.
common_indicators: The Bluetooth adapter is missing from Device Manager.
The Bluetooth adapter displays a warning icon or error code.
Bluetooth pairing repeatedly fails despite the device being powered on and discoverable.
The installed Bluetooth driver is outdated, disabled, or corrupted.
Windows reports that no Bluetooth adapter is installed.

quiz.question: What information should you verify before downloading an approved Bluetooth driver?
answers: The exact computer model and Windows version
Whether the website offers the newest driver
quiz.correct_answer: The exact computer model and Windows version

notes: Reviewed for safe driver installation practices.
Approved drivers must originate from the device manufacturer or organization-approved repository.
